The issue is not with sharing a subset of blocks post 7639, it's building systems which rely on discovering such peers. If a client were to search the network for peers who continue to serve the whole history (heterogeneous history storage) they might have to search a long time. And when they find a peer who does, it's likely there are more people who wish to download from them. It just isn't a robust way to access history. excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: Isn’t 7542 still useful for clients that only have a partial set of blocks post-7639?  Also is there a risk with 7542 that clients will bias against connecting to peers without any blocks and thus make it harder for new nodes to join the network?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:
The issue is not with sharing a subset of blocks post 7639, it's building systems which rely on discovering such peers. If a client were to search the network for peers who continue to serve the whole history (heterogeneous history storage) they might have to search a long time. And when they find a peer who does, it's likely there are more people who wish to download from them.

It just isn't a robust way to access history. I think it is much better as a network to keep the data each node officially serves over p2p consistent and force clients to implement other history retrieval mechanisms
